intent.raw: Create a strategy for research about using ontology-vault and DAG for the GoldenQuill project, inspect lean-formalization for reusable groundwork, look for skills and agents, and adapt Paradigma's New Age of Research reference to grant writing.
intent.objective: Plan a governed research route that maps GoldenQuill grant-writing knowledge into an ontology-backed DAG model with explicit node, edge, authority, validation, and promotion boundaries.
intent.operator_sentence: Use ontology-vault plus a DAG knowledge model to research how GoldenQuill can structure grant-writing claims, evidence, objections, replications, and reuse decisions.

route_menu.context_hint: The request needs a research strategy, not immediate production mutation. The selected route maps existing GoldenQuill and Arcanum surfaces first, then tests a toy grant graph before promotion.

items.label: Ontology DAG research
items.description: Map GoldenQuill grant-writing knowledge as candidate DAG nodes and edges using Ontology Vault branch-aware conventions.

items.label: Groundwork fanout
items.description: Use role-bound lanes to inspect GoldenQuill memory/vault surfaces, Ontology Vault schema work, Lean-formalization agents, grant workflow, and DAG reference adaptation.

items.label: Toy case validation
items.description: Validate the proposed graph contract on a non-org demo RFA and demo project context before any production claim.

techniques.purpose: Translate the Paradigma DAG-of-research reference into grant-writing nodes, edges, replication checks, objections, and reuse decisions.
techniques.validation_note: Validated only when a toy grant case can represent claims, evidence, objections, reviews, and promotion boundaries without authority leakage.

technique_overlays.trigger: External reference treats DAG as the unit of research knowledge; user asks how to adapt it to grant writing.

techniques.purpose: Map research DAG primitives to GoldenQuill proposal workflow primitives.
techniques.validation_note: Requires a toy graph artifact and explicit source authority classes.

technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The synthesis must name node families, edge families, authority classes, and one demo validation path.

subagent_strategy.trigger: The research spans GoldenQuill memory/vault contracts, Ontology Vault branch-aware schema, Lean-formalization agent patterns, grant workflow semantics, validation gates, and an external DAG reference.
subagent_strategy.explanation: Separate lanes prevent the DAG analogy from flattening GoldenQuill's authority boundaries and make existing groundwork visible before proposing new architecture.
context: GoldenQuill already has memory, vault, card, skills, and evidence surfaces.
Ontology Vault has a validated branch-aware candidate schema but not production promotion authority.
Lean-formalization has reusable agent and skill patterns for keeping ontology, research closure, verification state, and prose separate.
The Paradigma reference makes DAG structure load-bearing for cumulative research; GoldenQuill needs an equivalent structure for grant-writing evidence and decisions.

roles.purpose: Map GoldenQuill memory, vault, card, evidence, and substrate contract surfaces.
roles.owns: GoldenQuill memory and evidence surface map

roles.purpose: Map GoldenQuill grant workflow nodes from Scout, Scribe, Editor, Judge, Red Team, Logician, and operator decisions.
Map Ontology Vault branch-aware candidate fields onto grant-writing meaning, system, operational, and bridge branches.
Extract reusable Lean-formalization agent and skill patterns for ontology/research/verification separation.
Translate the Paradigma DAG reference into grant-writing graph primitives and anti-overclaim constraints.
Define validation and toy-case acceptance checks for non-org demo fixtures.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Run the ontology/DAG grant research subagents now using only repository files, public/demo fixtures, and the supplied Paradigma reference?

steps.name: Frame scope and source authority
stop_conditions: Block if the research would require reading more than one org PROJECT_CONTEXT.md.
Flag any external-reference claim that is not separated from repository evidence.
Block any production schema or memory mutation during this strategy pass.

steps.name: Map existing GoldenQuill memory, vault, skill, and agent groundwork
stop_conditions: Flag candidate surfaces whose maturity is schema-scaffold, dormant, generated, proposal-only, or stale.
Block if generated/proposal-only state is treated as canonical source.

steps.name: Translate the external research-DAG reference into grant-writing primitives

techniques.purpose: Convert research DAG concepts into grant-writing node and edge candidates.
techniques.validation_note: The distillation must preserve the external reference as context, not source authority for GoldenQuill internals.

stop_conditions: Flag if the analogy implies automatic consensus without GoldenQuill approval or validation gates.
Block if the route claims Paradigma terminology as GoldenQuill canonical vocabulary.

steps.name: Run role-bound groundwork research lanes
convergence_criteria: Each lane cites concrete file paths or the external reference URL for every material claim.
Each lane separates observed evidence, inference, candidate convention, and promotion decision.
Each lane returns node/edge candidates or explicitly says none found.
Each lane records authority and maturity risks in residue.
stop_conditions: Block synthesis if material claims lack paths, handles, or source URLs.
Block if any lane reads private org context without explicit one-org authorization.
Flag if lanes disagree about whether a surface is production, candidate, dormant, or proposal-only.

steps.name: Synthesize the grant ontology DAG candidate

techniques.purpose: Produce a candidate grant DAG vocabulary and authority model.
techniques.validation_note: Synthesis must include node families, edge families, authority classes, owners, and non-promotion guardrails.

convergence_criteria: Name minimum grant DAG node families and edge families.
Map each family to candidate owner surfaces and authority classes.
Preserve Ontology Vault branch boundaries and GoldenQuill org-isolation boundaries.
Name promotion routes without granting promotion authority.
stop_conditions: Block if the synthesis promotes Ontology Vault, Inventory, card, lesson, or org memory changes.
Flag unresolved branch-label choices such as meaning versus business as candidate convention residue.

steps.name: Validate the candidate graph with a non-org toy grant case
convergence_criteria: Toy graph includes opportunity, evidence item, proposal claim, objection, review, and decision nodes.
Every claim has support, contradiction, or explicit evidence gap.
Every node has an authority class and allowed use.
No private org context or production memory mutation is used.
stop_conditions: Block if demo fixtures contain private org material.
Block if a generated toy node is treated as production memory.
Flag if the graph cannot represent an objection or contradiction without deleting the claim.

steps.name: Choose next route after research validation
convergence_criteria: Choose one of: continue ontology-vault convention design, implement toy fixtures via task-session, create feature-glossary, or defer behind decision-gate.
Record unresolved authority decisions before implementation.
Do not proceed to production memory, card, or org-vault mutation without owner approval.
stop_conditions: Block if the selected route requires signed card, lesson, ontology, Inventory, or org memory mutation without explicit approval.
Defer if the toy validation cannot satisfy source-authority and org-isolation checks.

gates.condition: Research uses repository-level and demo/public fixtures only unless one explicit org context is authorized.
Every candidate node family and source surface has an authority class before reuse or promotion is discussed.
Research outputs do not promote Inventory, Ontology, glossary, skill, card, lesson, org memory, or GoldenQuill production contracts.
A non-org toy graph must represent claims, evidence, objections, reviews, decisions, and allowed uses before implementation work begins.
Recommended subagent fanout requires explicit user permission before runtime execution.

boundaries.contract: External reference may inspire DAG structure but cannot define GoldenQuill source truth or production vocabulary.
Branch-aware schema is a validated candidate surface only; it does not mutate GoldenQuill, Inventory, templates, or canonical ontology.
Toy validation uses demo/public fixtures and returns evidence artifacts without writing production memory or org vault state.

authority.lifecycle: dispatch-spec for route shape; ontology-vault for candidate ontology mapping; GoldenQuill owners for production adoption
authority.validation: dispatch-spec validator plus experiment-harness toy validation
authority.evidence: path-cited repository files and supplied external URL
authority.memory: GoldenQuill memory owners; research outputs are non-authoritative until approved
authority.promotion: no promotion authority in this dispatch

state_namespaces.write_policy: research artifacts only unless operator approves implementation
no read or write in this route unless one explicit org is authorized

promotion_splits.target: GoldenQuill production memory, signed card, lesson, or org vault
promotion_splits.rule: Research may propose candidates; owner approval and validation are required before mutation.

promotion_splits.target: canonical Ontology Vault or GoldenQuill schema
promotion_splits.rule: Candidate schema can be pressure-tested but not promoted by this dispatch.

promotion_guardrails: This dispatch creates a research strategy and candidate model only.
It does not promote Ontology Vault schema fields into GoldenQuill production.
It does not promote Inventory, glossary, sigil, spell, lesson, signed card, or org memory.
It does not authorize private org context reads.
It requires toy validation before implementation.
